question: In naive autoregressive generation, what is recomputed at every step?
options: The entire prefix, even though earlier positions have not changed
explanation: Calling model(ids) on the full sequence reprocesses every earlier position, whose results are identical to the previous step.

question: Why do the keys and values of earlier positions stay the same when a new token is added in a GPT?
options: The causal mask means each position depends only on itself and earlier tokens
Keys and values are frozen parameters
The new token is always padding
explanation: Because of causal masking, adding a token at the end cannot change any earlier hidden state, so their K and V can be reused.

question: During a decode step with a KV cache, what is the shape of the attention scores for one head?
options: 1 x (t+1): one query against all cached keys plus the new one
explanation: Only the new position needs an output, so there is a single query row attending over all t+1 keys.

question: What bug appears if you forget to offset positions by the cache length during decode?
options: Every new token is embedded as if it were at position 0, so outputs silently degrade
The cache grows twice as fast
explanation: With learned or rotary positions, the new token must use its absolute position P + t; otherwise the model sees the wrong order.

question: A model has 32 layers, 8 KV heads of 128 dims, and you cache 4096 tokens in fp16. How big is the cache per sequence?
What does grouped-query attention change?
options: Several query heads share one key/value head, reducing cache size
It caches the MLP outputs as well
explanation: Fewer KV heads means proportionally fewer cached keys and values, with little loss in quality.
